322	def effective_requirement(req: Requirement, amendments: list[calc.Amendment] | None = None,
323	                          reserves: dict[str, Decimal] | None = None,
324	                          scenario_date: date | datetime | None = None) -> EffectiveRequirement:
325	    """
326	    Hooks for the other workers' facts: scoped amendments from the tender Q&A (already filtered to the right sender
327	    by the caller; revision and requirement scoping and latest-wins happen here) and the per-end reserve values of
328	    the revision-specific Technikfreigabe, by reserve key. Without a needed reserve the stroke stays open.
329	    """
330	    base: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {"bore": req.bore, "stroke": req.stroke, "pressure": req.pressure,
331	                                      "mounting": req.mounting, "certification": req.certification}
332	    # An amendment names the revision its own way (label word, date or status around the identifier or not).
333	    scoped = [a.model_copy(update={"revision": req.revision}) if same_revision(a.revision, req.revision) else a
334	              for a in amendments or []]
335	    attrs = calc.apply_amendments(base, scoped, req.revision, req.requirement_id, scenario_date)
336	    pending: list[str] = []
337	    stroke: Decimal | None = Decimal(str(attrs["stroke"]))
338	    if req.stroke_is_usable:
339	        reserve = (reserves or {}).get(req.reserve_key or "")
340	        if reserve is None:
341	            pending.append(f"per-end reserve for key {req.reserve_key or '(none given)'}")
342	            stroke = None
343	        else:
344	            stroke = calc.nominal_stroke(stroke, Decimal(str(reserve)))
345	    pieces = req.pieces_per_set
346	    if "pieces_per_set" in attrs:  # an amended set size (rule 14) replaces the spec's for the Satz conversion
347	        try:
348	            pieces = parse_pieces_per_set(format(attrs["pieces_per_set"], "f")
349	                                          if isinstance(attrs["pieces_per_set"], Decimal) else attrs["pieces_per_set"])
350	        except ParseError as error:
351	            pending.append(f"amended pieces per set unreadable ({error})")
352	    return EffectiveRequirement(requirement_id=req.requirement_id, catalog_group=req.catalog_group,
353	                                bore=Decimal(str(attrs["bore"])), stroke=stroke,
354	                                pressure=Decimal(str(attrs["pressure"])), mounting=str(attrs["mounting"]),
355	                                certification=str(attrs["certification"]), pieces_per_set=pieces or None,
356	                                pending=pending)

363	    """A search hit with the attributes the list (or its detail page) shows."""

390	    material_number: str
391	    active: bool
392	    status: str = ""
393	    bore: Decimal | None = None
394	    stroke: Decimal | None = None

396	    mounting: str = ""

401	    production_lead_time_weeks: int | None = None

418	        return calc.Material(material_number=self.material_number, free_stock=self.free_stock or 0,
419	                             stock_lead_time_weeks=self.stock_lead_time_weeks,

426	class RequirementResearch(BaseModel):

428	    requirement_id: str
429	    search_term: str = ""
430	    candidates: list[Candidate] = Field(default_factory=list)
431	    inspected: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
432	    selected: str | None = Field(default=None, description="The exactly matching active material, if any")
433	    problems: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

438	def group_without_hits(searches: list[dict], group: str) -> bool:
439	    """
440	    Whether a catalogue group's search is definitively empty, from the searches a worker ran (site_tools records
441	    query, rows and whether the site showed its own no-hits notice): no search listed any row, at least two
442	    searches showed the notice, and one of them searched for the group itself. A search that merely found nothing
443	    to read (a wrong field, a page that did not load) never counts.
444	    """
445	    key = calc.norm_code(group)

447	        return False
448	    notices = [s for s in searches if s.get("no_hits")]
449	    return len(notices) >= 2 and any(key in calc.norm_code(s.get("query", "")) for s in notices)

452	def merged_attributes(record: MaterialRecord, research: RequirementResearch) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
453	    """A material's attributes: the detail page's where it showed them, else the search list's."""
454	    cand = next((c for c in research.candidates if c.material_number == record.material_number), None)
455	    attrs = cand.attributes() if cand else {}

466	    """Rule 3 as a validator: the attributes in which a material differs from the requirement (or does not show)."""
467	    out = []
468	    for key, value in req.attributes().items():
469	        if key not in attrs:
470	            out.append(f"{key} not shown")
471	        elif not calc.matching_materials({key: value}, [("x", {key: attrs[key]})], keys=(key,)):
472	            out.append(f"{key} {attrs[key]} instead of {value}")
473	    return out

479	def wording_differences(req: EffectiveRequirement, attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str]) -> list[str]:
480	    """
481	    The text attributes in which a material differs from the requirement, when those are its only differences
482	    (every number equal, every attribute shown): the cases where only the wording may differ. [] otherwise.
483	    """
484	    want = req.attributes()
485	    if req.stroke is None or any(key not in attrs for key in want):
486	        return []
487	    differ = [key for key, value in want.items()
488	              if not calc.matching_materials({key: value}, [("x", {key: attrs[key]})], keys=(key,))]
489	    return differ if differ and all(key in TEXT_KEYS for key in differ) else []

492	def check_choice(req: EffectiveRequirement, research: RequirementResearch, materials: dict[str, MaterialRecord],
493	                 chosen: str | None) -> str | None:
494	    """
495	    Validate a model's material choice; None when it holds, else why not. A chosen material must be inspected,
496	    active and equal in every attribute; "none" must not leave out an active material that equals in every one.
497	    """
498	    if chosen:
499	        record = materials.get(chosen)
500	        if record is None:
501	            return f"{chosen} is not among the inspected materials {sorted(materials)}"
502	        if not record.active:
503	            return f"{chosen} is not active (status {record.status})"
504	        diff = mismatches(req, merged_attributes(record, research))
505	        return f"{chosen} does not match exactly: {'; '.join(diff)}" if diff else None
506	    fits = [n for n, r in materials.items() if r.active and not mismatches(req, merged_attributes(r, research))]
507	    return f"{', '.join(fits)} is active and equals the requirement in every attribute; check again" if fits else None

511	                      material: MaterialRecord | None, pieces_per_set: int | None = None,
512	                      **extra) -> calc.PositionInput:
513	    """One position for calc: quantity in its stated unit (from the tender worker), pieces per set (an amended value
514	    from `effective_requirement` when given, else the spec's), the ERP material and its price conditions. `extra`
515	    passes the Q&A/mail facts (discount_scope, setup_fee, packaging, commitment) through."""
516	    return calc.PositionInput(

518	        pieces_per_set=pieces_per_set or requirement.pieces_per_set,
519	        material=material.to_material() if material else None,

"""
Evidence records the research workers produce, and their mapping onto calc's input models.

Workers copy values exactly as the pages show them (raw strings, which the grounding check can verify); the parsing
here is deterministic: locale-tagged numbers ("1.234,50 (de-DE)", "12,345 (en-US)"), dates in several orders,
masses with units, lead times in weeks. Exact attribute matching is a validator over the model-collected facts.
"""
import re
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

import calc

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parsing


class ParseError(ValueError):
    pass


_TAG = re.compile(r"\(\s*([a-z]{2})[-_]([A-Z]{2})\s*\)")
_NUM = re.compile(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'   ]*")


def number_format(text: str, fallback: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The locale a value is written in: its own tag "(de-DE)", else the fallback (e.g. the record's format)."""
    tag = _TAG.search(text or "")
    if tag:
        return tag.group(1).lower()
    if fallback:
        m = re.search(r"([a-z]{2})(?:[-_][A-Za-z]{2})?", fallback.strip(), re.IGNORECASE)
        return m.group(1).lower() if m else None
    return None


def parse_number(text: str, fmt: str | None = None) -> Decimal:
    """
    A number as a page writes it. `fmt` is a language code or locale ("de", "en-US") when the text carries no tag.

    Without any format: both separators -> the last one is decimal; a single comma or dot followed by exactly three
    digits is a thousands separator only for "en"/"de" respectively, otherwise German pages default to comma decimal.
    """
    if text is None:
        raise ParseError("no value")
    lang = number_format(text, fmt)
    body = _TAG.sub("", str(text))
    m = _NUM.search(body)
    if not m:
        raise ParseError(f"no number in {text!r}")
    raw = re.sub(r"['   ]", "", m.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    if lang == "en":
        raw = raw.replace(",", "")
    elif lang in ("de", "fr", "es", "it", "nl", "pt"):
        raw = raw.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif "," in raw and "." in raw:
        if raw.rfind(",") > raw.rfind("."):
            raw = raw.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
        else:
            raw = raw.replace(",", "")
    elif "," in raw:
        raw = raw.replace(",", ".") if raw.count(",") == 1 else raw.replace(",", "")
    elif raw.count(".") > 1:
        raw = raw.replace(".", "")
    try:
        return Decimal(raw)
    except InvalidOperation as error:
        raise ParseError(f"cannot read {text!r}") from error


def parse_int(text: str, fmt: str | None = None) -> int:
    value = parse_number(text, fmt)
    if value != value.to_integral_value():
        raise ParseError(f"{text!r} is not a whole number")
    return int(value)


_SET_WORDS = ("satz", "sätze", "saetze", "set", "kit", "pack")


def parse_pieces_per_set(text: str) -> int:
    """
    Pieces in one set, from a model's copy of the spec wording: "5", "5 Stück", or a definition such as
    "1 Satz = 5 Stück" / "2 sets = 10 pcs" (the first number there is the sets, not the pieces: a live run read 1
    and bid 26 pieces instead of 130). An equation gives right / left; otherwise a number next to a set word is the
    set count and the other one the pieces. Raises ParseError when the text does not say it unambiguously.
    """
    body = _TAG.sub("", str(text or ""))
    numbers = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\d+", body)]
    if len(numbers) == 1:
        return numbers[0]
    if len(numbers) == 2:
        sets, pieces = numbers
        equation = re.fullmatch(r"\D*\d+\D*[=:]\D*\d+\D*", body)
        if not equation:
            words = re.findall(r"(\d+)\s*([^\W\d_]*)", body)
            is_set = [w.casefold().startswith(_SET_WORDS) for _, w in words]
            if is_set == [False, True]:
                sets, pieces = numbers[1], numbers[0]
            elif is_set != [True, False]:
                raise ParseError(f"pieces per set unclear in {text!r}")
        if sets > 0 and pieces % sets == 0:
            return pieces // sets
    raise ParseError(f"pieces per set unclear in {text!r}")


_DATE_TAG = re.compile(r"\((MM|TT|DD)[/.-](TT|DD|MM)\)", re.IGNORECASE)


_MONTHS = {
    "januar": 1, "jänner": 1, "jaenner": 1, "january": 1, "jan": 1, "februar": 2, "february": 2, "feb": 2,
    "märz": 3, "maerz": 3, "march": 3, "mär": 3, "mrz": 3, "mar": 3, "april": 4, "apr": 4, "mai": 5, "may": 5,
    "juni": 6, "june": 6, "jun": 6, "juli": 7, "july": 7, "jul": 7, "august": 8, "aug": 8, "september": 9,
    "sept": 9, "sep": 9, "oktober": 10, "october": 10, "okt": 10, "oct": 10, "november": 11, "nov": 11,
    "dezember": 12, "december": 12, "dez": 12, "dec": 12}
_MONTH = "(" + "|".join(sorted(map(re.escape, _MONTHS), key=len, reverse=True)) + r")(?![^\W\d_])\.?"


def _year(text: str) -> int:
    """A four-digit year as is; a two-digit one in this century ("27" -> 2027)."""
    return int(text) + 2000 if len(text) == 2 else int(text)


def parse_date(text: str) -> date:
    """
    A date as shown: ISO "2027-01-25", German "25.01.2027" / "25.01.27", slashed "01/25/2027" / "25/01/27" with an
    optional order tag "(MM/TT)" / "(TT/MM)" that may stand between day-month and year ("21/03 (TT/MM) 2030"), or
    with a German or English month name ("25. Januar 2027", "25 Jan 27", "January 25, 2027"). Two-digit years are
    this century's. Untagged slashed dates are read day first unless that is impossible.
    """
    t = str(text)
    m = re.search(r"(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})", t)
    if m:
        return date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
    m = re.search(r"(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4}|\d{2})(?!\d)", t)
    if m:
        return date(_year(m.group(3)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(1)))
    m = re.search(r"(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})(?:/|\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*)(\d{4})(?!\d)", t) or \
        re.search(r"(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})/(\d{2})(?!\d)", t)
    if m:
        a, b, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), _year(m.group(3))
        tag = _DATE_TAG.search(t)
        month_first = bool(tag and tag.group(1).upper() == "MM") or (not tag and a <= 12 < b)
        month, day = (a, b) if month_first else (b, a)
        return date(year, month, day)
    low = t.casefold()
    m = re.search(r"(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})\.?\s*" + _MONTH + r",?\s*(\d{4}|\d{2})(?!\d)", low)
    if m:
        return date(_year(m.group(3)), _MONTHS[m.group(2)], int(m.group(1)))
    m = re.search(r"(?<![^\W\d_])" + _MONTH + r"\s*(\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th|\.)?,?\s*(\d{4}|\d{2})(?!\d)", low)
    if m:
        return date(_year(m.group(3)), _MONTHS[m.group(1)], int(m.group(2)))
    raise ParseError(f"no date in {text!r}")


_MASS_UNITS = {"kg": Decimal(1), "g": Decimal("0.001"), "t": Decimal(1000), "mg": Decimal("0.000001")}


def parse_mass_kg(text: str, fmt: str | None = None) -> Decimal:
    """A mass per piece in kg ("1250 g/Stück" -> 1.25). A bare number is taken as kg."""
    value = parse_number(text, fmt)
    unit = re.search(r"\d\s*(kg|mg|g|t)\b", _TAG.sub("", text), re.IGNORECASE)
    return value * _MASS_UNITS[unit.group(1).lower()] if unit else value


_WORKING_DAYS = re.compile(r"arbeitstag|werktag|working\s*days?|business\s*days?|work\s*days?",
                           re.IGNORECASE)


def parse_weeks(text: str) -> int:
    """
    A lead time in whole weeks ("3 Wochen", "3 weeks"). Days convert only when they make whole weeks: working days
    ("Arbeitstage", "Werktage", "business days") at 5 a week, calendar days at 7; anything else (months, a day count
    that is not whole weeks) raises, so the lead time stays unknown instead of wrong.
    """
    value = parse_number(text)
    if _WORKING_DAYS.search(text):
        per_week = 5
    elif re.search(r"tag|day", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        per_week = 7
    elif re.search(r"monat|month", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        raise ParseError(f"{text!r} is in months, not weeks")
    else:
        per_week = 1
    if value % per_week or value != value.to_integral_value():
        raise ParseError(f"{text!r} is not whole weeks")
    return int(value / per_week)


NONE_WORDS = re.compile(r"^(|-|—|–|keine?( gefordert| erforderlich| angegeben)?|ohne|none|n/?a|n\.\s?a|"
                        r"nicht gefordert)$", re.IGNORECASE)
# "No requirement" phrased in words: a negation followed by words only ("keine Zertifizierung", "ohne Zertifikat",
# "no certification", "without"), or a phrase saying it is not needed or does not apply ("nicht erforderlich",
# "not required", "entfällt"). A value with a digit is never taken as none.
_NEGATION = re.compile(r"^(keine?[nrms]?|ohne|no|none|without)(\s+[^\W\d_][^\s\d]*){0,3}$")
_NOT_NEEDED = re.compile(r"\b(nicht|not|kein|keine)\s+(erforderlich|gefordert|benötigt|benoetigt|notwendig|nötig|"
                         r"noetig|vorgeschrieben|zutreffend|anwendbar|required|needed|necessary|applicable|"
                         r"specified|requested)$|^(entfällt|entfaellt|unzutreffend|not applicable)$")


def norm_text(value: str | None) -> str:
    """Comparable form of a text attribute: case, spacing, ß, dashes; empty or "no requirement" wording becomes
    "none" ("-", "keine", "keine Zertifizierung", "ohne Zertifikat", "nicht erforderlich", "not required")."""
    t = " ".join(str(value or "").replace("ß", "ss").split()).strip(" .;").casefold()
    if NONE_WORDS.match(t):
        return "none"
    if not re.search(r"\d", t) and (_NEGATION.match(t) or _NOT_NEEDED.search(t)):
        return "none"
    return t


_CURRENCIES = {"€": "EUR", "eur": "EUR", "euro": "EUR", "euros": "EUR", "$": "USD", "us$": "USD", "usd": "USD",
               "us-dollar": "USD", "us dollar": "USD", "dollar": "USD", "dollars": "USD", "£": "GBP", "gbp": "GBP",
               "pfund": "GBP", "pound": "GBP", "pounds": "GBP", "britisches pfund": "GBP", "chf": "CHF",
               "sfr": "CHF", "franken": "CHF", "schweizer franken": "CHF", "swiss franc": "CHF",
               "swiss francs": "CHF", "¥": "JPY", "jpy": "JPY", "yen": "JPY", "yuan": "CNY", "renminbi": "CNY",
               "rmb": "CNY", "zloty": "PLN", "złoty": "PLN", "zł": "PLN"}


def parse_currency(text: str | None) -> str:
    """
    An ISO currency code from a page's wording: "€", "Euro" -> EUR; "$", "US-Dollar" -> USD; "£", "Schweizer
    Franken", ...; a code written in the text ("EUR (Euro)") is taken as is. '' when none is given; an unknown word
    comes back upper-cased in full (never cut to three letters, so it cannot pose as another code).
    """
    t = " ".join(str(text or "").split()).strip(" .:;()")
    if not t:
        return ""
    low = t.casefold()
    if low in _CURRENCIES:
        return _CURRENCIES[low]
    code = re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[A-Z]{3}(?![A-Za-z])", t)
    if code:
        return code.group(0)
    for word, iso in sorted(_CURRENCIES.items(), key=lambda kv: len(kv[0]), reverse=True):
        if re.search(rf"(?<![^\W\d_]){re.escape(word)}(?![^\W\d_])", low):
            return iso
    return t.upper()


REVISION_WORDS = {"revision", "rev", "index", "version", "ausgabe", "stand", "issue", "änderungsstand",
                  "aenderungsstand", "änderungsindex", "aenderungsindex"}


def _revision_tokens(text: str | None) -> list[str]:
    tokens = [t.strip(".-/") for t in re.findall(r"[\w./-]+", str(text or "").casefold())]
    return [t for t in tokens if t and t not in REVISION_WORDS]


def revision_id(text: str | None) -> str:
    """The identifier inside a revision label, comparable across sources: one source writes "Revision C of
    1 March", another just "C" or "Rev. C". The first token that is not a label word, without case."""
    return next(iter(_revision_tokens(text)), "")


def same_revision(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two labels of one revision: the same identifier, or a bare identifier that is a whole word of the other
    label. Whole words only: "A" is not inside "Revision B (aktuell)", "I" is not "III"."""
    ta, tb = _revision_tokens(a), _revision_tokens(b)
    if not ta or not tb:
        return False
    return ta[0] == tb[0] or (len(ta) == 1 and ta[0] in tb) or (len(tb) == 1 and tb[0] in ta)

class EffectiveRequirement(BaseModel):
    """The attributes an ERP material must match, after amendments and the usable-travel derivation (rules 14, 20)."""
    requirement_id: str
    catalog_group: str
    bore: Decimal
    stroke: Decimal | None = Field(description="Nominal stroke to match; None while a usable-travel reserve is "
                                               "still unknown")
    pressure: Decimal
    mounting: str
    certification: str
    pieces_per_set: int | None = Field(default=None, description="After amendments; None = as the spec says")
    pending: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="What is still unresolved")

    def attributes(self) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
        attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {"bore": self.bore, "pressure": self.pressure,
                                           "mounting": norm_text(self.mounting),
                                           "certification": norm_text(self.certification)}
        if self.stroke is not None:
            attrs["stroke"] = self.stroke
        return attrs


def effective_requirement(req: Requirement, amendments: list[calc.Amendment] | None = None,
                          reserves: dict[str, Decimal] | None = None,
                          scenario_date: date | datetime | None = None) -> EffectiveRequirement:
    """
    Hooks for the other workers' facts: scoped amendments from the tender Q&A (already filtered to the right sender
    by the caller; revision and requirement scoping and latest-wins happen here) and the per-end reserve values of
    the revision-specific Technikfreigabe, by reserve key. Without a needed reserve the stroke stays open.
    """
    base: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {"bore": req.bore, "stroke": req.stroke, "pressure": req.pressure,
                                      "mounting": req.mounting, "certification": req.certification}
    # An amendment names the revision its own way (label word, date or status around the identifier or not).
    scoped = [a.model_copy(update={"revision": req.revision}) if same_revision(a.revision, req.revision) else a
              for a in amendments or []]
    attrs = calc.apply_amendments(base, scoped, req.revision, req.requirement_id, scenario_date)
    pending: list[str] = []
    stroke: Decimal | None = Decimal(str(attrs["stroke"]))
    if req.stroke_is_usable:
        reserve = (reserves or {}).get(req.reserve_key or "")
        if reserve is None:
            pending.append(f"per-end reserve for key {req.reserve_key or '(none given)'}")
            stroke = None
        else:
            stroke = calc.nominal_stroke(stroke, Decimal(str(reserve)))
    pieces = req.pieces_per_set
    if "pieces_per_set" in attrs:  # an amended set size (rule 14) replaces the spec's for the Satz conversion
        try:
            pieces = parse_pieces_per_set(format(attrs["pieces_per_set"], "f")
                                          if isinstance(attrs["pieces_per_set"], Decimal) else attrs["pieces_per_set"])
        except ParseError as error:
            pending.append(f"amended pieces per set unreadable ({error})")
    return EffectiveRequirement(requirement_id=req.requirement_id, catalog_group=req.catalog_group,
                                bore=Decimal(str(attrs["bore"])), stroke=stroke,
                                pressure=Decimal(str(attrs["pressure"])), mounting=str(attrs["mounting"]),
                                certification=str(attrs["certification"]), pieces_per_set=pieces or None,
                                pending=pending)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- ERP


class Candidate(BaseModel):
    """A search hit with the attributes the list (or its detail page) shows."""
    material_number: str
    link: str = ""
    bore: Decimal | None = None
    stroke: Decimal | None = None
    pressure: Decimal | None = None
    mounting: str = ""
    certification: str = ""
    description: str = ""

    def attributes(self) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
        attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {"mounting": norm_text(self.mounting),
                                           "certification": norm_text(self.certification)}
        for key in ("bore", "stroke", "pressure"):
            if getattr(self, key) is not None:
                attrs[key] = getattr(self, key)
        return attrs


def matches(req: EffectiveRequirement, attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str]) -> bool:
    """Rule 3 as a validator: every resolved attribute equal (numbers as numbers, texts normalised)."""
    want = req.attributes()
    return bool(calc.matching_materials(want, [("x", attrs)], keys=tuple(want)))


class MaterialRecord(BaseModel):
    """Everything the ERP shows for one material that the bid needs, parsed."""
    material_number: str
    active: bool
    status: str = ""
    bore: Decimal | None = None
    stroke: Decimal | None = None
    pressure: Decimal | None = None
    mounting: str = ""
    certification: str = ""
    free_stock: int | None = None
    blocked_stock: int | None = None
    stock_lead_time_weeks: int | None = None
    production_lead_time_weeks: int | None = None
    pieces_per_carton: int | None = None
    allocation_mass_kg: Decimal | None = None
    surcharge_mass_kg: Decimal | None = None
    metal_index: str | None = None
    conditions: list[calc.PriceCondition] = Field(default_factory=list)
    raw: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    problems: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    def attributes(self) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
        return Candidate(material_number=self.material_number, bore=self.bore, stroke=self.stroke,
                         pressure=self.pressure, mounting=self.mounting,
                         certification=self.certification).attributes()

    def to_material(self) -> calc.Material:
        """The material for calc. A lead time not read stays None: calc fails only a position that needs it (stock
        or production, by pooled demand), and that position is omitted, never taken for a missing material."""
        return calc.Material(material_number=self.material_number, free_stock=self.free_stock or 0,
                             stock_lead_time_weeks=self.stock_lead_time_weeks,
                             production_lead_time_weeks=self.production_lead_time_weeks,
                             pieces_per_carton=self.pieces_per_carton,
                             allocation_mass=self.allocation_mass_kg or Decimal(0),
                             surcharge_mass=self.surcharge_mass_kg or Decimal(0), metal_index=self.metal_index)


class RequirementResearch(BaseModel):
    """ERP findings for one requirement: what was searched, the candidates, and the matching active material."""
    requirement_id: str
    search_term: str = ""
    candidates: list[Candidate] = Field(default_factory=list)
    inspected: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    selected: str | None = Field(default=None, description="The exactly matching active material, if any")
    problems: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    no_hits: bool = Field(default=False, description="The catalogue group search was complete and empty: the site "
                                                     "itself said there are no hits (searched, no match)")


def group_without_hits(searches: list[dict], group: str) -> bool:
    """
    Whether a catalogue group's search is definitively empty, from the searches a worker ran (site_tools records
    query, rows and whether the site showed its own no-hits notice): no search listed any row, at least two
    searches showed the notice, and one of them searched for the group itself. A search that merely found nothing
    to read (a wrong field, a page that did not load) never counts.
    """
    key = calc.norm_code(group)
    if not key or not searches or any(s.get("rows") for s in searches):
        return False
    notices = [s for s in searches if s.get("no_hits")]
    return len(notices) >= 2 and any(key in calc.norm_code(s.get("query", "")) for s in notices)


def merged_attributes(record: MaterialRecord, research: RequirementResearch) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
    """A material's attributes: the detail page's where it showed them, else the search list's."""
    cand = next((c for c in research.candidates if c.material_number == record.material_number), None)
    attrs = cand.attributes() if cand else {}
    for key in ("bore", "stroke", "pressure"):
        if getattr(record, key) is not None:
            attrs[key] = getattr(record, key)
    for key in ("mounting", "certification"):
        if getattr(record, key):
            attrs[key] = norm_text(getattr(record, key))
    return attrs


def mismatches(req: EffectiveRequirement, attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str]) -> list[str]:
    """Rule 3 as a validator: the attributes in which a material differs from the requirement (or does not show)."""
    out = []
    for key, value in req.attributes().items():
        if key not in attrs:
            out.append(f"{key} not shown")
        elif not calc.matching_materials({key: value}, [("x", {key: attrs[key]})], keys=(key,)):
            out.append(f"{key} {attrs[key]} instead of {value}")
    return out


TEXT_KEYS = ("mounting", "certification")


def wording_differences(req: EffectiveRequirement, attrs: dict[str, Decimal | str]) -> list[str]:
    """
    The text attributes in which a material differs from the requirement, when those are its only differences
    (every number equal, every attribute shown): the cases where only the wording may differ. [] otherwise.
    """
    want = req.attributes()
    if req.stroke is None or any(key not in attrs for key in want):
        return []
    differ = [key for key, value in want.items()
              if not calc.matching_materials({key: value}, [("x", {key: attrs[key]})], keys=(key,))]
    return differ if differ and all(key in TEXT_KEYS for key in differ) else []


def check_choice(req: EffectiveRequirement, research: RequirementResearch, materials: dict[str, MaterialRecord],
                 chosen: str | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Validate a model's material choice; None when it holds, else why not. A chosen material must be inspected,
    active and equal in every attribute; "none" must not leave out an active material that equals in every one.
    """
    if chosen:
        record = materials.get(chosen)
        if record is None:
            return f"{chosen} is not among the inspected materials {sorted(materials)}"
        if not record.active:
            return f"{chosen} is not active (status {record.status})"
        diff = mismatches(req, merged_attributes(record, research))
        return f"{chosen} does not match exactly: {'; '.join(diff)}" if diff else None
    fits = [n for n, r in materials.items() if r.active and not mismatches(req, merged_attributes(r, research))]
    return f"{', '.join(fits)} is active and equals the requirement in every attribute; check again" if fits else None


def to_position_input(position: str, quantity: int, unit: str | calc.Unit, requirement: Requirement,
                      material: MaterialRecord | None, pieces_per_set: int | None = None,
                      **extra) -> calc.PositionInput:
    """One position for calc: quantity in its stated unit (from the tender worker), pieces per set (an amended value
    from `effective_requirement` when given, else the spec's), the ERP material and its price conditions. `extra`
    passes the Q&A/mail facts (discount_scope, setup_fee, packaging, commitment) through."""
    return calc.PositionInput(
        position=position, quantity=quantity, unit=unit if isinstance(unit, calc.Unit) else calc.parse_unit(unit),
        pieces_per_set=pieces_per_set or requirement.pieces_per_set,
        material=material.to_material() if material else None,
        conditions=material.conditions if material else [], **extra)

153	REF_LINE = re.compile(r'\[(e\d+) (\w+) "([^"]*)"')
154	REFS = re.compile(r"\be\d+\b")
155	REF = re.compile(r"e\d+")
156	LINK = re.compile(r'\[(e\d+) link "([^"]*)" -> ([^\]\s]+)\]')
157	EMPTY_FRAME = re.compile(r"\[frame ([^\]\s]+)\]\n\[/frame\]")

160	def _normal(view: str) -> str:
161	    return REFS.sub("", view)

164	@dataclass
165	class Collected:
166	    pages: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
167	    control: tuple[str, str] | None = None  # (kind, name) of the list's paging control, once collect_pages ran
168	
169	    def add(self, view: str) -> bool:
170	        """Keep a page view; False when it adds nothing new (past the end a list repeats a page it showed)."""
171	        new = _normal(view)
172	        earlier = [_normal(p) for p in self.pages]
173	        if new in earlier:
174	            return False
175	        if earlier and set(earlier[-1].splitlines()) <= set(new.splitlines()):  # "load more" grew the list
176	            self.pages[-1] = view
177	            return True
178	        self.pages.append(view)
179	        return True
180	
181	    @property
182	    def text(self) -> str:
183	        return "\n\n".join(f"=== page view {i + 1}\n{p}" for i, p in enumerate(self.pages))
184	
185	
186	def _control(view: str, ref: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
187	    for r, kind, name in REF_LINE.findall(view):
188	        if r == ref:
189	            return kind, name
190	    return None

193	def record_views(session: SiteSession) -> list[str]:
194	    """Every distinct page text the session shows from now on, in order."""
195	    views: list[str] = []
196	    known: set[str] = set()
197	    look = session.look
198	
199	    async def recording_look(offset: int = 0, **options) -> str:
200	        out = await look(offset, **options)
201	        if offset == 0 and session.view and _normal(session.view) not in known:
202	            known.add(_normal(session.view))
203	            views.append(session.view)
204	        return out
205	
206	    session.look = recording_look  # type: ignore[method-assign]
207	    return views

210	def pages_to_read(collected: Collected, views: list[str], seen: str) -> list[str]:
211	    """
212	    The list pages to read: the collected ones first, then every other page of the same list the worker showed
213	    (a view with the list's paging control). collect_pages starts on the page the worker is on: in one sandbox run
214	    the worker had clicked "next" twice by hand before calling it, the first two pages were never read, and the
215	    amendment on them was lost (one position without a matching material, so the whole bid went in as no bid).
216	    """
217	    if not collected.pages:
218	        return [seen]
219	    have = {_normal(p) for p in collected.pages}
220	    extra = [v for v in views if _normal(v) not in have and collected.control is not None
221	             and any((k, n) == collected.control for _, k, n in REF_LINE.findall(v))]
222	    return [*collected.pages, *extra]

225	def paging_tool(collected: Collected):
226	    """A tool that pages through the result set the model is looking at, by repeating the control it names."""
227	
228	    async def collect_pages(ctx: RunContext[Deps], next_ref: str) -> str:
229	        """Collect the whole list you are looking at: give the ref of its "next page" or "load more" control. The
230	        control is clicked until the list ends; every page is kept for reading afterwards. Call it once, on the
231	        list's first page."""
232	        session: SiteSession = ctx.deps.session
233	        control = _control(session.view, next_ref)
234	        if control is None:
235	            return f"No control {next_ref} in the latest view; use a ref from the latest view."
236	        kind, name = control
237	        collected.control = control
238	        collected.add(session.view)
239	        ref, pages = next_ref, 1
240	        for _ in range(MAX_PAGES):
241	            before = _normal(session.view)
242	            await session.act("click", ref, _click)
243	            for _ in range(4):  # a list inside a frame can update a moment after the click settled
244	                if _normal(session.view) != before:
245	                    break
246	                await asyncio.sleep(0.7)
247	                await session.look()
248	            if not collected.add(session.view):
249	                break
250	            pages += 1
251	            same = [r for r, k, n in REF_LINE.findall(session.view) if k == kind and n == name]
252	            if not same:
253	                break
254	            ref = same[0]
255	        session.trace.event(session.name, "collect_pages", control=name, pages=len(collected.pages))
256	        session.trace.event(session.name, "collected", quiet=True, pages=collected.pages)
257	        text = collected.text
258	        if len(text) > MAX_RETURN:
259	            text = text[:MAX_RETURN] + f"\n[... {len(text) - MAX_RETURN} more characters, kept for reading]"
260	        return f"Collected {pages} page(s) of this list; they are kept for reading. The whole list:\n\n{text}"
261	
262	    return collect_pages

265	async def open_and_keep(session: SiteSession, urls: list[str], kept: list[str]) -> list[str]:
266	    """Open each chosen URL in a temporary tab of the session's browser context, side by side, and keep its text."""
267	
268	    async def one(url: str) -> str:
269	        tab = SiteSession(session.site, session.context, session.trace)
270	        page = await session.context.new_page()
271	        tab._watch(page)
272	        try:
273	            await tab._goto(url)
274	            view = await tab.look()
275	            # An embedded document that did not render in place (e.g. a lazy reading pane) is part of the chosen
276	            # page: open it on its own and add its text.
277	            for src in EMPTY_FRAME.findall(view)[:3]:
278	                await tab._goto(urljoin(url, src))
279	                view += f"\n[frame {src} opened]\n" + await tab.look()
280	            return view
281	        finally:
282	            await page.close()
283	
284	    views = await asyncio.gather(*(one(u) for u in urls), return_exceptions=True)
285	    good = [v for v in views if isinstance(v, str)]
286	    for view in good:
287	        kept.append(view)
288	        session.seen += "\n" + view
289	    return good

292	def _heads(views: list[str]) -> str:
293	    return "\n".join("- " + " / ".join(v.splitlines()[:2]) for v in views)

296	def keep_tool(kept: list[str]):
297	    """A tool that opens link targets the model chose, each in a temporary tab, and keeps their page text."""
298	
299	    async def keep_pages(ctx: RunContext[Deps], targets: list[str]) -> str:
300	        """Open these links and keep each page for reading afterwards: give each link's target (the "-> ..." part)
301	        or its ref from the latest view. Pass every page you want at once; they open side by side. Your own tab
302	        stays where it is."""
303	        session: SiteSession = ctx.deps.session
304	        host = urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc
305	
306	        def on_a_page(target: str) -> bool:  # chosen from a view, not made up
307	            url = urlparse(urljoin(session.page.url, target))
308	            local = url.path + (f"?{url.query}" if url.query else "")
309	            return target in session.seen or f"-> {local}" in session.seen or f"-> {url.geturl()}" in session.seen
310	
311	        links = LINK.findall(session.view)
312	        hrefs = {ref: href for ref, _, href in links}  # a link's ref from the latest view stands for its target
313	        targets = [hrefs.get(t.strip(), t.strip()) for t in targets]
314	        shown = [t for t in targets if t and not REF.fullmatch(t) and on_a_page(t)]
315	        unknown = [t for t in targets if t.strip() and t.strip() not in shown]
316	        urls = list(dict.fromkeys(urljoin(session.page.url, t) for t in shown))
317	        urls = [u for u in urls if urlparse(u).netloc == host][:25]
318	        good = await open_and_keep(session, urls, kept)
319	        session.trace.event(session.name, "keep_pages", targets=urls, unknown=unknown, kept=len(good))
320	        answer = f"Kept {len(good)} of {len(urls)} page(s):\n{_heads(good)}"
321	        if unknown:
322	            listing = "\n".join(f"  {ref}: {href}" for ref, _, href in links[:40])
323	            answer += (f"\nNot opened, these targets appear on no page you have seen: {unknown[:10]}. Use link "
324	                       f"targets exactly as the views show them. Links in the latest view:\n{listing}")
325	        return answer
326	
327	    return keep_pages

334	def keep_results_tool(kept: list[str]):
335	    """A tool that opens the result links whose visible text the model names, from every list the worker saw."""
336	
337	    async def keep_results(ctx: RunContext[Deps], link_texts: list[str]) -> str:
338	        """Open every result link whose visible text is exactly one of `link_texts` (e.g. a message subject as a
339	        result list shows it), from all result lists you have seen (all folders and pages), and keep each opened
340	        page for reading. Copy the texts exactly: a text with any extra characters is a different record."""
341	        session: SiteSession = ctx.deps.session
342	        host = urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc
343	        wanted = {_clean(t) for t in link_texts if t.strip()}
344	        hits = [href for _, text, href in LINK.findall(session.seen) if _clean(text) in wanted]
345	        urls = list(dict.fromkeys(urljoin(session.site["url"], h) for h in hits))
346	        urls = [u for u in urls if urlparse(u).netloc == host][:20]
347	        good = await open_and_keep(session, urls, kept)
348	        session.trace.event(session.name, "keep_results", texts=link_texts, urls=urls, kept=len(good))
349	        if not urls:
350	            texts = sorted({text for _, text, _ in LINK.findall(session.view)})[:40]
351	            return (f"No link seen with exactly these texts: {link_texts}. Link texts in the latest view: {texts}")
352	        return f"Kept {len(good)} of {len(urls)} result page(s):\n{_heads(good)}"
353	
354	    return keep_results

386	POSITIONS_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
387	You read the documents of a public tender and list its positions exactly as written: position number,
388	short text, quantity, unit and the requirement id of the buyer's specification the position refers to. Use the
389	ORIGINAL quantities the tender documents were published with; later changes are not part of this. If several documents list the positions, they should agree; prefer a table of the bill of
390	quantities. List every position once."""
391	
392	
393	QA_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
394	You read the bidder Q&A of a public tender and record every fact it states, exactly as written.
395	The answers may be shown out of number order (sorted by date); each answer has a number and a date. Use the
396	answer's own date (prefer the UTC timestamp shown, e.g. in a tooltip). One answer can carry several facts: record
397	each of them, with that answer's number and date. Record what the answers say; do not resolve conflicts, do not
398	skip older or superseded answers, and do not invent facts for positions an answer does not name. Statements that
399	a position is NOT a member of a pool or plan mean no membership: record nothing for them. An answer that withdraws
400	(zieht zurück) an earlier answer is a withdrawal of that earlier answer's number. Technical amendments name a
401	specification revision and a requirement: record one amendment per changed attribute. Copy numbers exactly as
402	written; do not convert them. The same answer can appear on two page views; record it once. Ignore page furniture (navigation, notices, buttons)."""
403	
404	
405	def _numbers(text: str) -> set[Decimal]:
406	    found: set[Decimal] = set()
407	    for token in re.findall(r"\d[\d.,]*", text):
408	        token = token.rstrip(".,")
409	        for candidate in (token.replace(",", "."), token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."), token.replace(",", "")):
410	            try:
411	                found.add(Decimal(candidate))
412	            except InvalidOperation:
413	                pass
414	    return found

417	def ungrounded(record: BaseModel, text: str, skip: tuple[str, ...] = ("date",)) -> list[str]:
418	    """Values in a record (numbers, keys) that the source text does not contain; dates are not checked."""
419	    numbers = _numbers(text)
420	    flat = " ".join(text.split())
421	    missing: list[str] = []
422	
423	    def check(value, name: str) -> None:
424	        if name in skip or value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, datetime)):
425	            return
426	        if isinstance(value, BaseModel):
427	            for k, v in value:
428	                check(v, k)
429	        elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
430	            for v in value:
431	                check(v, name)
432	        elif isinstance(value, dict):
433	            for k, v in value.items():
434	                check(v, str(k))
435	        elif isinstance(value, (int, Decimal, float)):
436	            if Decimal(str(value)) not in numbers:
437	                missing.append(f"{name}={value}")
438	        elif isinstance(value, str) and any(c.isdigit() for c in value):
439	            if " ".join(value.split()) not in flat and not (_numbers(value) and _numbers(value) <= numbers):
440	                missing.append(f"{name}={value!r}")
441	
442	    check(record, "")
443	    return missing

456	async def _read(output_type, instructions: str, text: str, prompt: str):
457	    agent = Agent(reader_model(), output_type=output_type, instructions=instructions,
458	                  model_settings=reader_settings(), retries=3)
459	
460	    @agent.output_validator
461	    def _grounded(records):
462	        missing = ungrounded(records, text)
463	        if missing:
464	            raise ModelRetry(f"These values are not in the pages: {', '.join(missing[:12])}. Copy values exactly.")
465	        return records
466	
467	    return (await agent.run(f"{prompt}\n\n{text}")).output

474	async def read_qa(pages: list[str], reference: str) -> QaRecords:
475	    """Each page view read on its own, in parallel (short answers, fast), then merged without duplicates."""
476	    parts = await asyncio.gather(*(_read(QaRecords, QA_INSTRUCTIONS, page, f"Tender {reference}. Bidder Q&A page:")
477	                                   for page in pages))
478	    merged = QaRecords(number_format=next((p.number_format for p in parts if p.number_format), ""))
479	    for name in QaRecords.model_fields:
480	        if name == "number_format":
481	            continue
482	        seen: dict[str, BaseModel] = {}
483	        for part in parts:
484	            for record in getattr(part, name):
485	                seen.setdefault(record.model_dump_json(), record)
486	        setattr(merged, name, list(seen.values()))
487	    return merged

490	async def research_tender(session: SiteSession, reference: str, scenario: datetime, *,
491	                          deadline: float | None = None, qa_session: SiteSession | None = None,
492	                          on_facts=None) -> TenderFacts | None:
493	    """
494	    Positions and Q&A of the tender, resolved per position. None when no positions were found.
495	
496	    With `qa_session` (a second tab of the website) the documents and the Q&A are worked side by side, each by its
497	    own worker. `on_facts(facts)` gets the positions with their original quantities as soon as they are read, so a
498	    deadline that comes before the Q&A still leaves them; the returned facts include the Q&A.
499	    """
500	    started = time.monotonic()
501	    if qa_session is None:
502	        return await _research_tender_one(session, reference, scenario, deadline=deadline, on_facts=on_facts)
503	    collected = Collected()
504	    documents: list[str] = []
505	
506	    async def positions_part() -> TenderPositions:
507	        await run_worker(session, _positions_goal(reference), Summary, deadline=deadline,
508	                         max_steps=steps_for(14, deadline), thinking=False, grounded=False,
509	                         tools=(keep_tool(documents),))
510	        return await read_positions("\n\n".join(documents or [session.seen]), reference)
511	
512	    async def qa_part() -> QaRecords:
513	        views = record_views(qa_session)
514	        await run_worker(qa_session, _qa_goal(reference), Summary, deadline=deadline,
515	                         max_steps=steps_for(14, deadline), thinking=False, grounded=False,
516	                         tools=(paging_tool(collected),))
517	        pages = pages_to_read(collected, views, qa_session.seen)
518	        if len(pages) > max(1, len(collected.pages)):
519	            qa_session.trace.event(qa_session.name, "list_pages_added", collected=len(collected.pages),
520	                                   added=len(pages) - len(collected.pages))
521	        return await read_qa(pages, reference)
522	
523	    qa_task = asyncio.create_task(qa_part())
524	    try:
525	        try:
526	            positions = await positions_part()
527	        except Exception as error:
528	            session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_positions_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:200])
529	            positions = TenderPositions(positions=[])
530	        if not positions.positions:  # the Q&A worker passed the tender's pages too
531	            await asyncio.wait([qa_task])
532	            try:
533	                positions = await read_positions(qa_session.seen, reference)
534	            except Exception:
535	                positions = TenderPositions(positions=[])
536	        if not positions.positions:
537	            session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_failed")
538	            return None
539	        fmt = positions.number_format or None
540	        if on_facts is not None and not qa_task.done():
541	            early = resolve_tender(positions.positions, QaRecords(), scenario, fmt)
542	            session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_positions", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1),
543	                                positions=[p.position for p in early.positions])
544	            on_facts(early)
545	        try:
546	            qa = await qa_task
547	        except Exception as error:
548	            session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_qa_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:200])
549	            qa = QaRecords()
550	    finally:
551	        if not qa_task.done():
552	            qa_task.cancel()
553	    facts = resolve_tender(positions.positions, qa, scenario, fmt)
554	    facts.seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
555	    session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_facts", seconds=facts.seconds,
556	                        positions=[p.model_dump(mode="json") for p in facts.positions], problems=facts.problems)
557	    if on_facts is not None:
558	        on_facts(facts)
559	    return facts
560

562	async def _research_tender_one(session: SiteSession, reference: str, scenario: datetime, *,
563	                               deadline: float | None = None, on_facts=None) -> TenderFacts | None:
564	    """Positions and Q&A by one worker in one tab."""
565	    started = time.monotonic()
566	    collected = Collected()
567	    documents: list[str] = []
568	    _, notes = await run_worker(session, _goal(reference), Summary, deadline=deadline,
569	                                max_steps=steps_for(20, deadline), thinking=False, grounded=False,
570	                                tools=(paging_tool(collected), keep_tool(documents)))
571	    if not documents:  # the worker read the documents in its own tab instead
572	        documents = [session.seen]
573	    qa_pages = collected.pages or [session.seen]  # without collect_pages: the answers it saw itself
574	    positions, qa = await asyncio.gather(read_positions("\n\n".join(documents), reference),
575	                                         read_qa(qa_pages, reference))
576	    if not positions.positions:
577	        session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_failed", notes=notes)
578	        return None
579	    facts = resolve_tender(positions.positions, qa, scenario, positions.number_format or None)
580	    facts.seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
581	    session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_facts", seconds=facts.seconds,
582	                        positions=[p.model_dump(mode="json") for p in facts.positions], problems=facts.problems)
583	    if on_facts is not None:
584	        on_facts(facts)
585	    return facts

597	    live = [r for r in records if _same_ref(r.position, position) and norm_id(r.answer_number) not in withdrawn

602	def _aware(value: datetime) -> datetime:
603	    return value if value.tzinfo else value.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
604	
605	
606	def _decimal_or_text(value: str, fmt: str | None) -> Decimal | str:
607	    try:
608	        return parse_number(value, fmt) if re.fullmatch(r"\s*[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s]*", value) else value.strip()
609	    except ParseError:
610	        return value.strip()
611	
612	
613	def resolve_tender(positions: list[TenderPosition], qa: QaRecords, scenario: datetime,
614	                   positions_format: str | None = None) -> TenderFacts:
615	    """
616	    Rules 1, 13, 14 and the Q&A keys: latest dated answer per position and key, withdrawn ones ignored. Position
617	    and answer numbers compare normalised ("Pos. 02" is "2"). A record that cannot be read costs only itself: an
618	    unreadable quantity change is left out, a position with an unreadable unit, quantity or fee is left out (it
619	    cannot be priced), and each is listed in `problems`.
620	    """
621	    scenario = _aware(scenario)
622	    withdrawn = {norm_id(w.withdrawn_number) for w in qa.withdrawals if _aware(w.date) <= scenario}
623	    fmt = qa.number_format or None
624	    problems: list[str] = []
625	    changes = []
626	    for c in qa.quantity_changes:
627	        if _aware(c.date) > scenario:
628	            continue
629	        try:
630	            changes.append(QuantityChange(number=c.answer_number, date=_aware(c.date), position=c.position,
631	                                          quantity=parse_int(c.quantity, fmt)))
632	        except (ParseError, ValueError) as error:
633	            problems.append(f"quantity change {c.answer_number} for position {c.position} unreadable: {error}")
634	    facts = []
635	    for p in sorted(positions, key=lambda p: position_key(p.position)):
636	        try:
637	            mine = [c for c in changes if _same_ref(c.position, p.position)]
638	            for c in mine:
639	                c.position = p.position
640	            original = parse_int(p.quantity, positions_format)
641	            final = resolve_quantity(original, p.position, mine, withdrawn, scenario)
642	            live = [c for c in mine if norm_id(c.number) not in withdrawn]
643	            source = max(live, key=lambda c: (c.date, position_key(c.number))).number if live else None
644	            fees = [f for f in qa.setup_fees if _same_ref(f.position, p.position)
645	                    and norm_id(f.answer_number) not in withdrawn and _aware(f.date) <= scenario]
646	            fee = parse_number(max(fees, key=lambda f: _aware(f.date)).amount, fmt) if fees else Decimal(0)
647	            facts.append(PositionFacts(
648	                position=p.position, short_text=p.short_text, requirement=p.requirement, unit=parse_unit(p.unit),
649	                unit_text=p.unit, tender_quantity=original, quantity=final, quantity_answer=source,
650	                condition_group=_latest_key(qa.condition_groups, p.position, withdrawn, scenario),
651	                packaging_key=_latest_key(qa.packaging_tariffs, p.position, withdrawn, scenario),
652	                commitment_key=_latest_key(qa.delivery_commitments, p.position, withdrawn, scenario),
653	                setup_pool_key=_latest_key(qa.setup_pools, p.position, withdrawn, scenario),
654	                bonus_key=_latest_key(qa.project_bonuses, p.position, withdrawn, scenario),
655	                setup_fee=fee))
656	        except (ParseError, CalcError, ValueError) as error:
657	            problems.append(f"position {p.position} left out: {error}")
658	    amendments = [Amendment(date=_aware(a.date), revision=a.revision, requirement=a.requirement,
659	                            attributes={a.attribute if a.attribute != "other" else a.attribute_label:
660	                                        _decimal_or_text(a.value, fmt)})
661	                  for a in qa.amendments if norm_id(a.answer_number) not in withdrawn and _aware(a.date) <= scenario]
662	    units = {a.attribute: a.unit for a in qa.amendments if a.unit}
663	    shown = sorted({w.withdrawn_number for w in qa.withdrawals if _aware(w.date) <= scenario})  # as written
664	    return TenderFacts(positions=facts, amendments=amendments, amendment_units=units, withdrawn=shown,
665	                       qa=qa, problems=problems)
